spans.s: + अप्यय लोक-ईश-प्रभव- + अप्यय, adj. owing both origin and end to the guardians of the world,
+ अभिहार लोक- + अभिहार, m. lustration of arms.
+ पाल लोक- + पाल, see s. v.

लोक-पाल, m.
 1. A king.
 2. The name of certain divinities, guardians of the world, as Indra, Soma, etc.; cf. a list of them in Wilson's Specimens of the Theatre of the Hindus, i. 2. ed. 219, n. ad Vikr. d. 36.
+ पितामह लोक- + पितामह, m. the great forefather of mankind.
+ प्रवाद लोक- + प्रवाद, m. common report or saying,
+ यात्रा लोक- + यात्रा, f. 1. the way of the world,
. traffic, intercourse, Hit. i. d. 104, M.
. the life of the world, Bhāg.
+ रञ्जन लोक- + रञ्जन, n. gaining public confidence.

लोक्, i. 1, Ātm., and i. 10, Par. (probably a denomin. derived from लोक),
 1. To see.
 2. i. 10, † To shine, to speak.
 --With the prep. अव अव, i. 1 and 10,
 1. To see,

; to see to, Śāk. 3, 6; to watch, Pañc. 249, 4.
 2. To perceive,

.
 --With समव सम्-अव, i. 10, To inspect, Śāk. d. 13.
 --With आ [] आ, i. 1 and 10,
 1. To look out,
. To regard, Vikr. d. 81; to see, Pañc. i. d. 21; to inspect, to view,

. To acknowledge, Pañc. pr. d. 3.
 --With वि वि, i. 10, To see,

. To take a view of, Pañc. 46, 7.
 3. To look over,

. To perceive, 2, 9.
 --Ptcple. of the pf. pass. विलोकित, n. Seeing, Śāk. d. 36.
 --With प्रवि प्र-वि, To look forward,

लोक, i. e. लोच्, or रुच्, + अ (with ल् for र्, cf. रुच्), m.
 1. Seeing, sight.
 2. The world, the universe,
. A world, a division of the universe,

(मध्यम, The middle world, i. e. the earth).
 4. Man, mankind.
 5. Men. people, sing. and pl., Daśak. in
लोकालोक, i. e. लोक-अ-, m. a mountainous belt bounding the world.
लोकायत, i. e. लोक-आ-यत (vb. यम्?), n. The system of atheistical philosophy, taught by चार्वाक.
लोकायतिक, लोकायत + इक, m. A follower of the Cārvāka system (see the last)
+ वाद लोक- + वाद, m. rumour, Daśak. in
+ वाह्य लोक- + वाह्य, m. an outcaste.
